THE MOVEMENT OF HOPE IN THE CHURCH

STATUTE

Movement of Hope

c/o Institute of the Daughters of St Anne

Via Merulana, 177 – 00185 Roma

Tel. 70.00642

OVERVIEW

Origins and Identity

1. The «Movement of Hope», so named since 24 May 1989, is rooted in the inspiration of Mother Rose Gattorno, who tried repeatedly to organise it in juridical form but did not succeed; it reappears, from 1924, as «Friends of the Association of the Daughters of St Anne»; it comes to the fore again and is given careful consideration during the Special Chapter of the religious Family of the Daughters of St Anne, in 1972 and 1978; it regains vigour and then gradually takes clearer shape, constituting itself as a Movement, beginning with the intuition of Rita Di Maggio who, during the solemn Celebration of 9 December 1981 on the occasion of the translation of the venerated mortal remains of the Servant of God Rose Gattorno from the Generalate House to the Church of St Anne at the Lateran, felt the impulse to spread Mother Rose’s charism among the laity.

With the definitive approval of the Religious Family (Gen. Chap. 1990) and the subsequent authoritative confirmation of the Church, the Movement is fully called to share in and to live out in the world the charism and the spirituality of the Daughters of St Anne.

Vocation to the Spirituality of the Movement

2. Gathered as a small part of the People of God, moved by the Holy Spirit to respond to a free calling of the Father, the Movement strives so that the divine plan of salvation may reach, ever more each day, all people of all times and of the whole earth, collaborating in the Church in the saving Work of Christ, in the attitude of poverty of heart and self-giving that was proper to St Anne.

3. In deepening and living its own vocation-mission, the Movement makes its own the theological and spiritual foundations of the Spirituality of the Family of the Daughters of St Anne — direct heirs of the charism of Mother Rose Gattorno — drawing them from their Constitutions and from the Documents of the Institute.

St Anne

4. Mother of the Mother of the Redeemer, and therefore placed in a particular way within the history of Salvation, St Anne represents a sign of that spirituality of expectation which, in total self-emptying and loving openness towards God and towards one’s neighbour, was characteristic of the little Remnant of Israel. Therefore, although St Anne’s belonging to the chosen people and her privilege of being the Mother of Mary are the only elements we are given to know about her person and her life, they are sufficient to deduce the message on which the particular spirituality of the Movement is founded.

Sign of Hope

5. The calling in the Movement consists in bearing witness to the world of the whole meaning of the Hope-Covenant of the Remnant of Israel, which:

– bases its life on God’s fidelity to his promises;

– remains faithful to the commitments of the Covenant;

– understands its contents in an ever more spiritual way;

– progressively overcomes the limit of waiting for material goods;

– awaits the fulfilment of God’s promises;

– is certain that he will remember his mercy.

For this reason, relying on the historical experience of God, of his Love and of his forgiveness, the Remnant of Israel walks with God and is conscious of his infinite transcendence and of his unforeseeable irruption into history.

6. The expectation of the Remnant of Israel is characterised by constant openness to the newness of God, which is revealed by the gradual fulfilment of what «he promised to Abraham and to his posterity for ever».

It is therefore a hope that gains strength from the experience of the Covenant of the Remnant of Israel which, in Mary, contemplates the Dawn of the new day of salvation.

Mary

7. Deeply set in the very heart of salvation and associated with the Messiah, the one awaited by the nations, Mary becomes the fulfilment and the new hope of the world. In her the members of the Movement contemplate God’s first response to the hope of the poor, of the «faithful remnant», among whom Anne and Joachim stand out, who deserved to have so great a Daughter because of their poverty of heart and their hope.

8. Mary is the new Israel, the daughter of Zion, with whom the Lord of life and of history plans the new and eternal Covenant: the entrance into the world of the Messiah, the one awaited by the nations, the Saviour, the Restorer, the Servant of Yahweh, the Redeemer.

The Servant of Yahweh

9. The Father willed to accomplish the redemption of humankind through a «Poor One» who, sharing the condition of poverty of fallen humanity, fulfilled his mission without splendour, with gentleness, and, apparently, with a failure which God, by his infinite power, transformed into salvation for all.

Such is the likeness of the «Poor One» that the prophet Isaiah outlines under the figure of the Servant of Yahweh.

His Mission

10. He lived poor among the poor, and it was chiefly to the poor that he directed his teaching and his «good news»; he explicitly proclaimed his identification with them, in a presence that will last until the end of time, and he ended his earthly life in the supreme humiliation and poverty of the cross.

11. From this death life is born for humankind, and poverty is changed into resurrection.

The Servant becomes Lord: «…and I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all men to myself»; and «therefore God has highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name which is above every name…».

Vocation and Mission of the Movement

12. Docile to this call, the Movement presents itself to the world as a sign of expectation and of gift: expectation of the return of Christ in glory, and gift to God in service to our brothers and sisters, in an effort towards an ever greater identification with that attitude of poverty which Mary, Daughter of St Anne, expressed in the Magnificat; which Christ, Servant of Yahweh, lived in his earthly life and exalted in the beatitudes; and which Mother Rose, moved by the Holy Spirit, has handed down.

With the Confirmation of the Church

13. The approval given by the Ecclesiastical Authority firmly places the Movement within the life and the holiness of the Church.

PURPOSE AND SPIRITUALITY OF THE MOVEMENT

14. The purpose of the calling of the laity in the Movement of Hope is to walk towards holiness by following Christ in the mystery of his poverty, in order to collaborate, in the Church, in his saving work, under the guidance of St Anne, Mother of Mary Immaculate.

Rooted, through the Holy Mother of Mary, in the Spirituality of the «Poor of Yahweh», the members of the Movement follow Christ the «poor one» par excellence, and, contemplating Mary who «stands out among the lowly and poor of the Lord», they live their baptismal consecration in the poverty of heart which becomes for them the way of being, of living and of existing that qualifies their presence in the world and shapes their style of life.

Poverty of heart which Mother Rose embodied in her own existence, driven by her ardent desire, even when she was still a lay woman, to identify herself with the Christ who emptied himself even to death on a cross, with Him whom she used to call «my Good» and whose very path she longed to follow, with her gaze fixed on Mary as the perfect model of what she experienced as her most intimate vocation: «useless slave of my Jesus, my beloved Master» (Mother Rose).

15. Jesus Christ continues his mystery of salvation in the Church, and in the Church, consequently, «every man», reborn of water and the Spirit, will be able to reach the fullness of his vocation in Christ; a vocation which he will realise by fulfilling, in his own particular state of life, the mission entrusted to him by the Father.

16. The Christian vocation is, by its very nature, also a vocation to the apostolate, so that love for God is completed and consummated in love for our brothers and sisters.

In a Climate of Communion

17. The response to one and the same calling gives life to the Movement of Hope, characterised internally by a family style of life whose inspiring model is the family of St Anne.

In this family climate the members of the Movement live together their moments of prayer and formation, of meetings for the sharing of life and for fraternal communion… in the fundamental attitude of the poor: animated by faith, hope and charity, in simplicity and prudence, in humility and meekness, with solicitous dedication towards their brothers and sisters, beginning with their own families. In this way they continue the mission of the Holy Mother in the active expectation of the day of the Lord.

With the Attitude of the Poor, Animated by Faith…

18. The call addressed to Mother Rose Gattorno and, in her, to each member of the Movement, entails a deepening of baptismal consecration in a commitment of more intimate covenant with God, supremely beloved, and therefore demands an adherence of faith constantly renewed to Him who, calling from all eternity, continually manifests his Love.

Therefore, following the example of Mary, pilgrim of faith, the members of the Movement, conscious of their own littleness and open and docile to the Word of God, believe the divine message, welcome it and keep it in their hearts, and renew their response of faith to the Father, seeking to discover beneath the fabric of daily events the expression of his will, made concrete in the Person and work of the Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

19. And since believing in Christ necessarily implies believing the Church, the «pillar and bulwark of the truth», and «a sign and instrument of intimate union with God and of the unity of the whole human race», the members of the Movement commit themselves to ensuring that the Word of God may spread and be glorified and that the Kingdom may be proclaimed and established throughout the earth.

…by Hope…

20. Just as the Church, a community of hope, lives in the infallible certainty that the work of salvation «has already begun in Christ and is carried forward by the sending of the Holy Spirit», so the members of the Movement, called to share in this hope by virtue of their Christian vocation, live in the presence of the Lord, in the joyful certainty that God is their only inheritance.

21. God, who animates human history from within, is the Hope of Israel.

In this God St Anne and Saint Joachim placed their hope. In this hope they formed their daughter, Mary.

To this hope Mother Rose and Fr Tornatore refer in their teaching on abandonment and trust in God.

22. The members of the Movement walk towards Christ, seeking the Kingdom of God and his righteousness; and, abandoning themselves to Him, sure that «in everything God works for good with those who love him», they accept to share in the paschal mystery of Christ, knowing that «the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed».

23. Their hope is therefore the Risen Christ.

It passes through the understanding and love of Christ Crucified, in whom all the ancient promises are illuminated and surpassed, and the future finds its foundation and the strength for a commitment to «hope against hope» on the part of all those who are crucified by various afflictions.

…and by Charity

24. The Church, «established by Christ as a communion of life, charity and truth», represents and brings about the communion of the faithful with the Redeemer in the unity of a single body and, rooted and grounded in love, is the sign of the intra-trinitarian life which Christ came to manifest to the world.

25. In Christ the love of God reaches us personally. It is Christ who makes us discover concretely and vitally the love of God: «As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you»; a personal love, because, even within the communal vocation of the people of God, it is expressed in an individual election; a love which culminates in the supreme sign of death on the cross» and which remains in us by the power of the Spirit, making us able to imitate the charity of Christ.

26. To be in love means also to act in love: «If you keep my commandments, you will abide in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commandments and abide in his love».

27. To do the Father’s will is Christ’s response of love and is therefore also the sign that verifies identification with Him, the «poor one» who, in his total openness to the Father, made the divine will his own.

28. This attitude of openness, which excludes self-interest and seeks only the glory of the Lord, each member of the Movement must make his or her own and live in sincerity, humility, self-forgetfulness and self-giving, so that, with a thirst for the infinite, he or she may manifest «the charity with which God has loved the world».

THEY GROW IN THE PARTICULAR VIRTUES

…of Simplicity…

29. Simplicity, a reflection of the simplicity of God and a virtue proper to a poor heart, leads the members of the Movement to think, speak and act with uprightness and sincerity, and to shun all pretence and cunning, so that there may be harmony within them: «If your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light».

30. Far, therefore, from duplicity and prejudice, they open themselves to the truth which is revealed to the humble and the little ones, and they go out to meet their brothers and sisters in simplicity of heart, to announce to them, above all by the authenticity of their lives, this Truth, which is a bond of union and an essential condition of freedom.

…and Prudence

31. Simplicity, which «cannot live without the company of prudence», forms with it an inseparable pair which, sincerely lived, leads to the possession of true wisdom: «Be wise as serpents and innocent as doves». Christ is not only the Teacher who teaches the practice of this virtue, but his very person is the foundation of Christian prudence, because He is the sole and absolute criterion which enables us to discern and judge the different spirits, and thus to avoid being like children «tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine».

32. The members of the Movement root their prudence in Jesus Christ, following the example of Mother Rose who knows nothing but the Crucified; and, in the humble acknowledgement of their own reality, anchored in faith, they strive to discern in concrete situations the sign of God’s will and to interpret under that sign the true meaning and value of things. Thus oriented towards the building of the Kingdom, they bring about in themselves that continual growth which will bring them «to mature manhood, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ».

…Humility…

33. Identification with Christ the Poor One, the true fulcrum of the spirituality of the Movement, finds its most characteristic expression in humility, which is the cornerstone of the life and teaching of Jesus: «Learn from me; for I am gentle and lowly in heart». The humility of Christ is manifested as a filial attitude towards the Father and as a disposition of service towards our brothers and sisters.

34. To the essence of humility belong both the recognition of one’s own condition as a creature, a creature wounded by sin, and the knowledge of the sublime holiness of God; from this comparison springs the sentiment of gratitude and the adoring joy towards the infinite divine goodness: «As for me, I am poor and needy; but the Lord takes thought for me».

35. Nevertheless, humility is not a denial of one’s own abilities, but a sincere appraisal of the gifts received from God and of the duties they entail in relation to the service of our brothers and sisters: «As each has received a gift, employ it for one another, as good stewards of God’s varied grace». The use of these gifts in a selfish way, or as an object of vainglory, is thus excluded.

36. The members of the Movement, who are called by Christ to imitate this particular attitude of his by choosing the lowest places, serving as He himself did with all gentleness and kindness, and working for the extension of the Kingdom, conscious that the gifts received from God are for the common edification, must nevertheless make their own the words of the Gospel: «We are unworthy servants; we have only done what was our duty».

They must nurture these sentiments first of all in relation to their own family or the social environment in which they happen to live; let them not aspire to greatness but let themselves be drawn to what is lowly. This will be the best way of imitating St Anne who, from the humility of her anonymity, was exalted by God as the glorious Mother of the Mother of the Redeemer.

…and Meekness…

37. The virtue of meekness is the spontaneous radiation of humility and the way chosen by Jesus to proclaim the Kingdom.

Exercised with sincerity in the reality of daily encounters, it penetrates the hearts of people and makes them open and receptive to the gospel message, so that the words of Christ come true: «Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth».

38. Following the example of Christ, the meek Lamb, the members of the Movement, desirous of helping to gather the whole human family around the Father, must clothe themselves in «compassion, kindness, lowliness, meekness, patience», in the conviction that only disinterested goodness, which no one can gainsay, will contribute to the building of a new world, free from selfishness and pride.

…and in Active Dedication, like the Church, Bride and Mother

39. Charity towards God and towards our brothers and sisters impels the members of the Movement to give themselves with a love which, as a reflection of the merciful love of God, signifies and continues today the (maternal) mission of St Anne and makes them share vitally in the fruitfulness of the Church.

Such maternal love is a participation in the infinite richness of the Trinitarian life. God himself revealed to the children of Israel this dimension of his Love: «Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should have no compassion on the son of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you». And again: «As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you».

Thus every member of the Movement, in self-giving to others «in silent and hidden sacrifice» (Mother Rose), announces, prepares and awaits the day of the Lord, serving Christ in his members with that love of which Mary was in her life a shining example.

40. The poor heart of Mary, the exalted daughter of Zion, is the one that most faithfully mirrored the tenderness of that divine love «which surpasses knowledge»; and the Church, by contemplating and imitating Mary, herself becomes Mother, in the faithful and fruitful acceptance of the Word of God.

THE MEMBERS OF THE MOVEMENT LIVE IN CHARITY…

In the Spirit of the «Poor»

41. Following the example of Mother Rose, docile to the action of the Holy Spirit, the members of the Movement seek, in the intimacy of prayer, the encounter with the Father, in order to build with Him, in imitation of Christ, a relationship of tender and intense filial love.

Faithful to Jesus’ exhortation to pray without ceasing, and taking inspiration from the poor and lowly of the Lord who «with groans and sighs, tears and prayers» prepare the coming of the Messiah, the members of the Movement walk humbly with God, seeking his face in the secret of their hearts and in the fraternal exchange of a communion of prayer which has its centre in the Eucharist.

In this way, persevering in prayer with Mary the Mother of Jesus and proclaiming the death and the resurrection of the Lord, they prepare with the whole Church for his full manifestation: «Come, Lord Jesus».

They Nourish Prayer

42. The brothers and sisters of the Movement commit themselves to discovering day by day, in the intimacy of personal dialogue with God, his saving will, and to opening themselves to the action of the Spirit so as to become docile instruments of the Father’s mercy:

a) «I have no other treasure than prayer» (Mother Rose). Aware of this priceless spiritual patrimony of Mother Rose, the members of the Movement of Hope, taking inspiration from her charism, will cultivate prayer and the spirit of prayer, devoting themselves each day to personal reflection, whose essential nourishment will be Sacred Scripture;

b) the interiorisation of the Word is not possible without creating, within oneself and around oneself, a climate of silence, which allows us to listen to God who reveals himself as «a still small voice», speaks to the heart and says to his creatures: «Be silent and listen».

Gathered by the Word

43. In the dynamism of the interiorisation of the Word, the members of the Movement will have recourse to those most effective means which are:

a) the weekly celebration of the Word, as the manifestation of an ecclesial community that listens, meditates and responds with song and prayer in order then to put the divine message into practice in life;

b) the monthly retreat and the annual spiritual exercises, as times of fullness suited to restoring inner energies and apostolic zeal, in fidelity to the vocational identity of the Movement;

c) the study of Sacred Scripture, of the documents of the Church and of the Institute, as well as of other aids, as a means of growth in the sublime knowledge of Jesus Christ, so as to be ever more ready to respond to the demands of their own vocation and mission in the Church, according to their own state of life.

In a Need for Conversion

44. The members of the Movement, enlightened by the Word of God in the humble knowledge of themselves, experience the need for constant conversion.

This fundamental need will be expressed in the voluntary practice of some mortification, which will help them to free themselves from the leaven of selfishness, pride and sensuality; and, in the light of the paschal joy of the resurrection, it will be transformed into an effective will for salvation, for themselves and for all people.

To this end:

a) they will be careful to value, as means of redemption, perseverance in faithfulness to their duty, the difficulties inherent in their state of life and work, as well as sickness and every other suffering;

b) each group will choose some form of mortification suited, from time to time, to the spirit of the liturgical seasons, or to particular needs of the group itself, of the Institute, of the Church, of the homeland and of the whole world.

They Receive the Grace of Forgiveness

45. In order to follow Christ and to become ever more docile to the voice of the Spirit in a renewed encounter with the Father, the members of the Movement:

a) will approach the sacrament of Penance frequently, and will receive its grace not only for their own personal growth but also to restore the fraternal and ecclesial communion that has been wounded by sin;

b) will revive, as a community, the spirit of conversion and purification of heart by means of a penitential celebration at least during the main seasons of the liturgical year, in which, humbly acknowledging their individual and collective sin, they will be reconciled with one another and will express together the joy of God’s forgiveness, to the praise of his glory.

Strengthened by the Eucharist

46. The members of the Movement of Hope find in the Eucharist the full expression of what their journey must be: a unity of persons convoked by the Father, who is transformed by the Holy Spirit into the Body of Christ, for the glory of God and the salvation of the world.

It is also fidelity to the original spirit of the charism received by Mother Rose, which is eminently oriented towards the Eucharist;

a) the centre of the liturgical life of the group and of each member will be participation in the Eucharist, «Sacrament of the Sacrifice of the Redeemer»;

b) the members will show their love for the Word made flesh who came to dwell among us by visiting him often and by promoting moments of adoration, also in community.

Lovers of Mary

47. The members of the Movement contemplate Mary united to Jesus in the mystery of his redeeming poverty; through her life they also discover the figure and the message of Anne, her Holy Mother.

They celebrate her mysteries in the light of the history of salvation, entrusting to her motherly love their baptismal consecration and imploring her intercession for the whole pilgrim people;

a) may the Rosary, a compendium of the whole Gospel, be a prayer particularly loved by the members of the Movement;

b) may the solemnities and feasts of Mary be lived as particular moments of theological deepening of the person and mission of Mary;

c) they will strive to arouse and increase devotion to Mary.

In Communion with the Holy Mother

48. Among the saints who in the heavenly Church intercede for us before the Father, the Movement venerates in a special way the Holy Mother of Mary Immaculate, whose presence determines the particular character of its spirituality. Grateful to God for the gift of St Anne to the Institute and hence to the Movement, the members proclaim and praise her holiness:

a) by deepening and living the virtues proper to the spirituality;

b) by invoking her, they renew their trust in her motherly solicitude and entrust to her intercession their needs and those of the whole world;

c) by taking the most opportune occasions to present her figure and her message to those they meet, and by advising them to have recourse also to her «powerful help to obtain graces from God».

And with the Patron Saints

49. Considering themselves «as guarantors of the debt which all the faithful have of cherishing sentiments of love and gratitude towards that blessed couple…, whom God used to give the world the Mother of the Saviour», they will honour in a particular way Saint Joachim, father of Mary Most Holy. In addition they will welcome and make their own the devotion to Saint Joseph, spouse of the Virgin Mary, to Saint Michael the Archangel, to Saint Francis of Assisi and to Saint Francis of Paola, honouring them in the spirit of the liturgy.

ESSENTIAL PRACTICAL GUIDELINES

FORMATION

1. The members of the Movement meet weekly, for the journey of Christian, spiritual and charismatic formation, in the Parishes, or with the Sisters, or also in the homes or premises managed by the groups themselves.

2. It is the duty of all to acquire adequate Christian formation and to nourish their own spiritual life and their knowledge of the charism, by taking part in:

– the weekly celebration of the Word;

– periodic formation meetings;

– monthly retreats;

– annual Spiritual Exercises;

– Courses, Conferences, etc., organised by the Parish, by the Diocese, or by the religious family of the Daughters of St Anne.

APOSTOLIC COMMITMENT

a) Open to the reality of the local Church, the members of the Movement take their place in the Parish Community, working for the extension of the Kingdom, in communion with the Parish Priest and the other Parish and Diocesan Bodies, devoting themselves — according to their own possibilities — to liturgy, catechesis, Caritas, volunteer work and above all to the least of all.

b) Taking to heart, like Mother Rose, the primacy of Evangelisation for the «propagation of the faith», the members of the Movement also seek to reach — where possible — poor Parishes or areas lacking a Christian presence, in order to make Christ known.

c) Since the charism is a gift of God to the Church, the members of the Movement, directly or through the Sisters, should feel the joy and the urgency of announcing this gift to others, so that they too may undertake or intensify the journey of faith, rediscovering their own baptism and embracing the spirituality of the Movement.

To this end they work for the establishment and the specific formation of other groups.

STRUCTURES OF THE MOVEMENT

1. The Movement is guided by a central team and by provincial teams composed of:

– at least two lay people

– a woman religious, Daughter of St Anne

– a Presbyter

2. The members of the Movement meet in groups headed by a leader, assisted by the Sister Daughter of St Anne, for the transmission of the charism, and, where possible, are spiritually guided by a Presbyter.

3. The leader will be elected by the members of the group, or appointed by the central or provincial team, on the basis of the journey made in the Movement, of his or her serious commitment to growth in faith and in the witness of Christian life, of his or her capacity to create communion among the members and to live concretely a sense of belonging to the group.

4. Provision is made for the rotation of the Leader or his or her replacement, in case of need, or for other emerging reasons.

5. Among the groups, according to the possibilities of times and places, there should be an exchange of experiences, to grow in faith and to strengthen the sense of belonging to the Movement; furthermore, the members should live in communion with the Religious Family of the Daughters of St Anne, sharing in their spiritual benefits, sharing their concern for the Kingdom, and feeling themselves part of one great Family.

PERSONS WHO BELONG TO IT

The Movement is open to all the faithful who wish to make a journey of faith with this spirituality: adolescents, young people, adults, the elderly, widows, couples, families and presbyters.

WAYS OF ENTERING

For membership of the Movement, after an adequate period of experience in the group, each member officially takes up the Statute and the badge, as a sign of his or her own faith and of belonging to the Movement.
